seasonRead.headline: 2013–14: Cycle pressure gives the season its shape
paragraphs: The 2013–14 model learned 6 forward styles. Cycle Pressure Play-Driver led with 242 of 467 forwards (51.8%), followed by Two-Way Shot-Share Driver at 28.9%.

The leading pair accounts for 80.7% of forwards, with Cycle Pressure Play-Driver holding the larger lane. The final three styles combine for only 5.6%, leaving cycle pressure and two-way shot-share play as the defining split.

seasonRead.headline: 2013–14: Puck movement and shot blocking share the stage
paragraphs: The 2013–14 model learned 5 defense styles. Play-Driving Puck-Moving Defenseman led with 93 of 246 defenders (37.8%), followed by Shot-Blocking Defensive Defenseman at 30.9%.

The gap between Play-Driving Puck-Moving Defenseman and Shot-Blocking Defensive Defenseman is 6.9 points, while 15.0% sits outside the top three. The model reads the blue line as a contest between advancement and defensive detail, not a one-style season.
